subject.title: [Feature]: Add $EDITOR compose mode in TUI (external editor handoff) for multiline prompts

question: Should OpenClaw add a core TUI external-editor compose mode, and if so which trigger and temp-file/local-process safeguards are required?
rationale: The feature is aligned with TUI ergonomics, but it executes an environment-selected local editor and stores prompt text in a temporary file, so automation should not choose the permanent UX or security boundary alone.

options.title: Approve Guarded TUI Compose Mode
options.body: Implement the external-editor handoff in the TUI composer with a maintainer-approved shortcut or slash command, secure temp-file handling, inherited stdio while suspended, no auto-send, tests, and docs.

options.title: Defer Until Editor Boundary Is Settled
options.body: Keep the request open but wait for a broader TUI keymap/editor ownership decision before adding another composer path.

options.title: Decline Core Editor Handoff
options.body: Close or narrow this request if maintainers decide local editor spawning should remain outside OpenClaw core despite the ergonomic benefit.

recommendation.title: Approve Guarded TUI Compose Mode
recommendation.body: Implement the external-editor handoff in the TUI composer with a maintainer-approved shortcut or slash command, secure temp-file handling, inherited stdio while suspended, no auto-send, tests, and docs.
